text:
ashwin: quick follow-up from the slab-based KV + attention kernel RFC. saw two edgecases in local testing that we should decide on before the kernel selection patch lands

mia: yup, saw a couple as well. which ones?

ashwin: 1) when the KV is fragmented across many small slab ranges the kernel currently falls back to the generic attention path and fetches the whole KV. that kills latency for long contexts. 2) eviction race: a page eviction can compact and change offsets while the kernel is mid-request, leading to incorrect KV indices.

sabrina: for (1) are we sure it's the fallback policy that's the problem vs our RMU defrag heuristics? iirc the heuristic threshold is 6 ranges, but most real workloads hit 10+ tiny runs after prefix-cache churn.

jon: agree. our metric showed ~14% of requests had >8 ranges under bursty prefix patterns. fallback -> generic path adds ~2.4ms median token latency in the hot path.

mia: proposal: add a lightweight kv_hint proto in the runtime request header. fields: contiguous_ranges[], total_cached_length, eviction_epoch. kernel will use kv_hint to decide if partial-KV path is safe.

ashwin: sketch of kv_handshake header we've been experimenting with: ```
kv_handshake: {
  flags: CONTIG_OK | PARTIAL_OK,
  max_ranges: 4,        // kernel will only accept partial fetches up to this many ranges
  page_size_bytes: 65536,
  eviction_epoch: 1623
}
```

jon: two comments: (a) max_ranges should be dynamic per-request based on model batch size and latency SLO, (b) we need a reject code that indicates WHY kernel rejected partial path so the router can retry with adjusted config instead of blind fallback.

mia: +1. propose kernel reject codes: PARTIAL_TOO_FRAGMENTED, EVICTION_CONFLICT, NOT_SUPPORTED. router can map PARTIAL_TOO_FRAGMENTED -> try_coalesce=1, or route to Dedicated.

perf-bot: perf-run:kv-slab/primers v3 finished: contiguous hit rate 78% (baseline 60%), p50 token latency delta -0.8ms when partial-KV allowed. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/v/kv-slab-v3

ashwin: nice. that perf number makes a strong case. but eviction race still worries me. we need a commit-compare handshake with an epoch and a small per-range checksum to detect midfetch moves.

sabrina: checksum per-range ok but must be cheap. propose simple 64-bit xxhash over range header (start,len,slot_version). kernel validates checksums on arrival. if mismatch -> EVICTION_CONFLICT.

jon: could also attach a signed eviction token when eviction finishes: `EPOCH:1623:SIG`. Router includes it; kernel rejects stale tokens. helps with cross-node eviction since routers have latest control-plane view.

mia: agree. here's a minimal flow I want to standardize: 
1) router computes contiguous_ranges and epoch+checksums and sends kv_handshake.
2) kernel returns ACCEPT(max_ranges=N) or REJECT(code) with optional adjust_hint.
3) if ACCEPT, router issues partial-KV fetch ranges; kernel validates checksums and epoch before applying.
4) if mismatch, kernel responds with EVICTION_CONFLICT and router falls back or retries after requerying control plane.

ashwin: sounds good. can we add a fast-path for single-range short prefixes where we skip checksums to avoid overhead? add flag NO_CHECKSUM_ALLOWED for very low-latency requests.

sabrina: dangerous but useful. require explicit opt-in from client API (must set low_latency=true). platform will log and count regressions.

mia: another compatibility point: attention kernels that rely on contiguous GPU tensors need guarantees about memory layout. we should expose a "layout_hint" indicating whether ranges are physically contiguous in GPU address space or logically contiguous but strided. kernel can then pick the right memory copy path.

ashwin: example layout_hint values: PHYS_CONTIGUOUS, LOGICAL_STRIDE, FRAGMENTED. router derives from slab allocator metadata.

jon: test plan: add unit tests that simulate concurrent evict+fetch with randomized delays, assert kernel either ACCEPTs and validates, or returns EVICTION_CONFLICT. add microbench harness to compare p50/p95 for PHYS_CONTIGUOUS vs FRAGMENTED.

perf-bot: microbench results attached to patch: phys_contig p50=0.62ms frag p50=2.9ms p95=8.1ms

sabrina: ok. if fragmentation penalty is that big we have to prefer coalescing heuristics in allocator. not all models can tolerate that p95.

ashwin: implementation notes: 
- router: compute ranges in O(n) per-request; attach up to 8 ranges in handshake. payload stays <1KB.
- kernel: expose api `handshake(request_id, kv_handshake_blob) -> { decision, max_ranges, reject_code, adjust_hint }`
- allocator: maintain per-range epoch and 64-bit checksum computed at free/commit time.

mia: code snippet for kernel API (pseudo): ```
// called before token gen starts
Decision kernel_handshake(RequestID rid, KVHandshake h) {
  if (!kernel_supports_partial) return {REJECT, NOT_SUPPORTED};
  if (h.max_ranges > KERNEL_MAX_RANGES) return {REJECT, PARTIAL_TOO_FRAGMENTED, {suggested_max: KERNEL_MAX_RANGES}};
  if (h.eviction_epoch < allocator.current_epoch()) return {REJECT, EVICTION_CONFLICT};
  return {ACCEPT, min(h.max_ranges, KERNEL_MAX_RANGES)};
}
```

jon: important: recording metrics for all rejections and adjust_hints so controller can tune defaults automatically. we should add `kv.handshake.rejects` taggable in telemetry.

ashwin: deployment plan: gate behind feature-flag for 2 weeks on canary. default conservative max_ranges=2. gather telemetry and then widen.

mia: PR pointers: router changes in https://git.redwood/r/r2/kv-router/pull/412, kernel handshake in https://git.redwood/r/r2/runtime/pull/897. I'll drop unit tests in both.

sabrina: one last thought: memory reclamation during GC may reassign slab slots but keep epoch unchanged if we do in-place compaction. that would break checksum approach. we need to ensure compaction bumps epoch or provides stable relocation map.

jon: agree. allocator must bump epoch on any address-affecting mutation. doc that constraint in allocator API.

ashwin: ok, plan sounds actionable. @mia can you draft the handshake proto and add the reject codes + telemetry hooks? we'll iterate in PRs.

mia: on it. drafting now, will add the tests and perf harness. assigning follow-ups in PR. :thumbsup:
